The AI Productivity Index (APEX)

paper.arxiv.2509.25721

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

The original APEX-v1.0 primary paper and the independently pinned creator APEX-v1-extended card describe one explicitly versioned APEX task/evaluation lineage. Three separate AI source-content review invocations bind each approved assertion at its exact scientific digest. Original hidden/public partitions, model/response/grader conditions, later extended protocol, source denominators and incompatible-looking use/license statements stay qualified. This is the retained finite-inventory APEX-1 target, newly admitted to this graph; it is distinct from the already recorded APEX-Agents and APEX Accounting families. No replicated results, current supplier performance assessment, source-document rights clearance, family duplication or finalized core eligibility is asserted.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · paper method: APEX-v1.0 grades each rubric criterion with three judges: o3 with thinking Low, Gemini 2.5 Pro with thinking Off, and Sonnet 4 with thinking Off. It uses a two-of-three or unanimous majority for each binary criterion grade.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.criterion-majority-judge.v3

  • A response score is the percentage of rubric criteria passed.
  • Appendix B sets temperature 0.01 for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Sonnet 4, leaves o3 temperature unset, and prompts for a binary result plus a concise explanation grounded in the response and criterion.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: The APEX-v1.0 paper compares its model scores with publicly reported HLE, MMLU Pro, MMMU Val and GPQA scores and reports a mean cross-benchmark correlation of 0.79.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.cross-benchmark-comparability.v3

  • Only 12 of 23 models have HLE scores, 12 have MMLU Pro scores, 13 have MMMU Val scores and 22 have GPQA scores; the authors state that missing scores limit robustness.
  • This is the paper authors' comparison of available reported benchmark scores, not a new execution of those benchmarks.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · paper method: The captured APEX-v1.0 paper parses evidence PDFs and CSVs with Reducto and appends the parsed material to each task prompt, using one parsing strategy across models and avoiding the closed models' native file-handling APIs.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.document-input-and-access.v3

  • The authors argue that models must receive the complete evidence documents for a fair APEX-v1.0 comparison; this is an in-context evaluation, not an evaluated document-retrieval workflow.
  • The experiment accessed 13 closed-source models through their APIs and ten open-source models through providers; those model-access channels are distinct from the expert-authored benchmark data.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: The APEX-v1.0 paper explicitly cautions that rubric scores need not track real-world value linearly: a response scoring 60% might be effectively useless when value is stage-gated.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.economic-value-interpretation.v3

  • The authors describe value as dependent on product and use context and leave cost and latency assessment to future work.
  • The hidden heldout design reduces contamination risk but cannot fully eliminate it, especially after public disclosure of the benchmark design.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: The APEX-v1.0 judge panel agrees with expert Pass/Fail labels on 89% of 5,818 criterion ratings collected for responses from one model, Gemini 2.5 Pro with thinking On.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.human-judge-validation-scope.v3

  • Those expert ratings were not validated by reviewers; the authors explicitly flag their greater risk of annotation error.
  • The paper reports judge-human agreement by domain ranging from 84.3% in law to 94.5% in management consulting; the 89% panel result remains scoped to the sampled model responses and expert labels.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: In APEX-v1.0, repeating each judge three times on responses from one arbitrarily selected model, Grok 4, yields reported internal agreement of 99.5% for o3 Low, 99.4% for Gemini 2.5 Pro Off and 99.6% for Sonnet 4 Off.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.judge-repeatability-scope.v3

  • This repeatability check uses the one selected model; it is not a measured error rate against expert truth.
  • Across the broader criterion-grading collection of over 400,000 data points, the three judges agree unanimously in 81.16% of cases, with majority voting used for the remainder.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · evaluates: In the captured APEX-v1.0 experiment, GPT 5 with thinking High has the highest reported mean score, 64.2%, followed by Grok 4 at 61.3% and Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking On at 60.4%.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.original-model-results.v3

  • These are reported results on the original 200-case heldout suite using median-of-three responses and the three-model criterion-majority judging protocol.
  • The mean score is the percentage of rubric criteria passed, not a percentage of tasks fully solved or of economic value delivered.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: APEX-v1.0 rubrics lack negative criteria that penalize incorrect or irrelevant statements, so passing many positive criteria does not guarantee that a response contains fewer errors.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.rubric-error-and-retrieval-limits.v3

  • The authors also identify measurement error from rubric construction, annotator calibration, run variability and LM judging, especially on complex technical criteria.
  • The setup supplies needed sources in context; the authors expect live work involving information search and tools to be harder.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · documents: The APEX-v1.0 observational comparison reports mean scores of 55.8% for models offering thinking tokens versus 40.4% for the others, with 16 of 23 models in the thinking group.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.thinking-comparison-limit.v3

  • Thinking models are more often closed source and newer, and the authors identify these as confounders; they do not establish a causal improvement from enabling thinking.
  • The paper says a reliable thinking-effect comparison would require on/off or high/low ablations and also declines reliable parameter-scaling claims because model details differ or are undisclosed.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

The AI Productivity Index (APEX) · paper method: APEX-v1.0 collects three responses from every model for each prompt and uses the median of their three scored responses for the leaderboard and analysis.

candidate.next8.apex.paper.three-run-median.v3

  • Across models, the mean within-prompt score range across the three runs is reported as 11.9 percentage points; the authors reject reporting the best run because it could favor more variable models.
  • The reported experiment covers 23 models, and the paper dates response collection to the start of August 2025; its scores are historical results under that setup.
